summary: Structurally valid and ontologically clean, file coverage with the LysC sibling is complete and disjoint, and the digest split is defensible; but fraction identifiers contradict the deposited file names for 31 of the 48 A53T-mutant runs, and the heavy SILAM reference rows carry the control factor level, merging the spike-in reference into the 'normal' condition.

findings.location: comment[fraction identifier], rows 106-123, 133-150 (A53T_mutant_rep1 f09a..f24) and 159-171, 180-192 (A53T_mutant_rep2 F12..F24); 62 rows / 31 files
findings.message: Fraction identifier is the file's position in its series, not the fraction. Mutant rep2 F12-F24 are labelled 9-21 and rep1 f10-f24 are shifted by 1-3, so fraction 9 means f09 in rep1 but F12 in rep2, and mutant fraction N no longer matches control fraction N.
findings.evidence: Deposited names carry the fraction number (Mouse_SILAM_A53T_mutant_rep2_Tryp_F12.raw -> fraction 9; ..._rep1_Tryp_f24.raw -> 27); rep2 has no suffixed files, so nominal numbers are already unique there. Paper: 24 concatenated fractions. Correction: every unsuffixed file carries the nominal number from its name (rep2 F12-F24 = 12-24; rep1 f10..f24 = 10..24); the three re-acquired files f09a/f10a/f11a get distinct identifiers that do not shift any other fraction, under a stated rule; uniqueness coordinate must still hold.

findings.message: The heavy SILAM spike-in reference (present in every run, including PD runs) carries factor level 'normal', the same level as the AAV1-GFP control arm, so the reference is counted as control samples.
findings.evidence: Producer's own convert-openms output: conditions normal=144 (48 GFP light + 96 reference heavy) vs PD=48. Paper quantifies each mouse relative to the SILAM reference (intensities divided by SILAM). Repository precedent PXD001364 gives the heavy reference factor values 'not applicable'. Correction: reference rows take a factor level that is not an experimental arm (e.g. 'not applicable'), characteristics[disease]=normal may stay; re-run validate-sdrf and convert-openms showing the reference outside the compared conditions.

findings.message: Split by digest is justified (LysC and Tryp series of the same mouse/rep are separately fractionated pools whose 1-24 fraction coordinates collide), but the manifest's 'cleavage agent holds one value per row' is not a constraint; rows can differ. Same fraction-position and reference-factor issues likely apply to the A53T rows of the LysC sibling (e.g. control rep2 LysC F09 missing).
findings.evidence: PRIDE file list; Methods sequential LysC -> trypsin on the 30 kDa filter.

findings.message: 'PrP-TetP-hA53T alpha-synuclein transgenic' is a genotype, not a strain; background is B6 (founders B6C3F2 crossed to B6).

'The entire amount was injected' conflicts with 'injected twice'; rep2 may be a second preparation of the same lysate rather than a re-injection. Value 2 is still a technical replicate of the same mouse.
